arguments.sql_query: SELECT ca.ancestor_concept_id, ac.concept_name AS ancestor_name, ca.descendant_concept_id, dc.concept_name AS descendant_name FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca JOIN omop.concept ac ON ac.concept_id=ca.ancestor_concept_id JOIN omop.concept dc ON dc.concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (4164770,374925) ORDER BY ca.ancestor_concept_id, dc.concept_name;

WITH gbs_concepts AS ( SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (4164770,374925) UNION SELECT concept_id FROM (VALUES (4164770),(374925),(37166081),(37164489),(35624130),(37204369)) v(concept_id) ), yearly AS ( SELECT YEAR(condition_start_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS gbs_dx, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS gbs_patients FROM omop.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_start_date >= '2017-01-01' AND condition_start_date < '2026-01-01' AND condition_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM gbs_concepts) GROUP BY YEAR(condition_start_date) ), totals AS ( SELECT YEAR(condition_start_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS all_dx, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS all_patients FROM omop.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_start_date >= '2017-01-01' AND condition_start_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(condition_start_date) ) SELECT t.yr, COALESCE(y.gbs_dx,0) AS gbs_dx, COALESCE(y.gbs_patients,0) AS gbs_patients, t.all_dx, t.all_patients, CAST(COALESCE(y.gbs_dx,0)*1000000.0/t.all_dx AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS gbs_dx_per_million_conditions, CAST(COALESCE(y.gbs_patients,0)*100000.0/t.all_patients AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS gbs_patients_per_100k_patients FROM totals t LEFT JOIN yearly y ON t.yr=y.yr ORDER BY t.yr;

(4164770),(374925),(37166081),(37164489),(35624130),(37204369)) v(concept_id) ), yearly AS ( SELECT YEAR(condition_start_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS gbs_dx, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS gbs_patients FROM omop.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_start_date >= '2017-01-01' AND condition_start_date < '2025-01-01' AND condition_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM gbs_concepts) GROUP BY YEAR(condition_start_date) ), totals AS ( SELECT YEAR(condition_start_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS all_dx, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS all_patients FROM omop.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_start_date >= '2017-01-01' AND condition_start_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(condition_start_date) ), yearly_rates AS ( SELECT t.yr, CASE WHEN t.yr BETWEEN 2017 AND 2019 THEN 'pre-pandemic' WHEN t.yr BETWEEN 2020 AND 2022 THEN 'pandemic' WHEN t.yr BETWEEN 2023 AND 2024 THEN 'post-pandemic' END AS period, COALESCE(y.gbs_dx,0) AS gbs_dx, COALESCE(y.gbs_patients,0) AS gbs_patients, t.all_dx, t.all_patients, COALESCE(y.gbs_dx,0)*1000000.0/t.all_dx AS dx_per_million_conditions, COALESCE(y.gbs_patients,0)*100000.0/t.all_patients AS patients_per_100k_patients FROM totals t LEFT JOIN yearly y ON t.yr=y.yr WHERE t.yr BETWEEN 2017 AND 2024 ) SELECT period, MIN(yr) AS start_year, MAX(yr) AS end_year, SUM(gbs_dx) AS gbs_dx, SUM(gbs_patients) AS yearly_patient_count_sum, SUM(all_dx) AS all_dx, SUM(all_patients) AS yearly_patient_denominator_sum, CAST(SUM(gbs_dx)*1000000.0/SUM(all_dx) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS pooled_dx_per_million_conditions, CAST(AVG(dx_per_million_conditions) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS mean_annual_dx_per_million_conditions, CAST(SUM(gbs_patients)*100000.0/SUM(all_patients) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS pooled_patients_per_100k_patients, CAST(AVG(patients_per_100k_patients) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS mean_annual_patients_per_100k_patients FROM yearly_rates GROUP BY period ORDER BY start_year;

content.text:
Using MedCP OMOP condition records, I defined Guillain-Barré syndrome as SNOMED `4164770` plus descendants and related acute infective polyneuritis concepts, then compared:

| Period | Years | GBS diagnoses | Pooled rate per 1M condition diagnoses | GBS patients per 100k patients |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pre-pandemic | 2017–2019 | 1,940 | 37.884 | 21.620 |
| Pandemic | 2020–2022 | 2,474 | 37.022 | 19.418 |
| Post-pandemic | 2023–2024 | 2,776 | 50.171 | 23.442 |

**Answer: No, not after normalization.**  
Although the raw number of GBS diagnoses was higher during 2020–2022 than 2017–2019, the overall diagnosis volume also increased. Normalized to all condition diagnoses, GBS frequency was **slightly lower during the pandemic than pre-pandemic** and **clearly lower than post-pandemic**.

So the data do **not** support a higher pandemic-period diagnosis frequency for Guillain-Barré syndrome relative to both pre- and post-pandemic periods.
